messages:
Maya: Heads-up — Acme reported intermittent SSE streams where the connection drops after a few partial chunks when their frontend is slow to read. They see lots of socket write errors server-side and duplicated reconnects that spike billing. They attached a snippet of the client's console logs.

Arjun: Can you paste the server-side error logs? sounds like backpressure hitting the runtime write path (EAGAIN/EPIPE) or the proxy buffering.

Maya: Pasted below from the customer's app (they're on us-east). They said it happens when they throttle the main UI thread.

Customer console (copied):
```
SSE: open
SSE: chunk received (partial)\nSSE: stalled processing for 2.5s
SSE: connection closed, reconnecting (status 0)
SSE: reconnect 1 -> 401
```

Maya: And here are our runtime logs around the disconnect timeframe: (trimmed)
```
2026-07-12T12:41:07.123Z runtime-1234 INFO handle_stream start req=abc123
2026-07-12T12:41:09.639Z runtime-1234 WARN socket write returned EAGAIN, blocking_count=3
2026-07-12T12:41:11.002Z runtime-1234 ERROR write failed: EPIPE at send_chunks() pid=42
2026-07-12T12:41:11.003Z runtime-1234 INFO aborting stream req=abc123 reason=slow_consumer
2026-07-12T12:41:11.010Z auth-svc INFO token invalidation check for session xyz
```

Tomas: That sequence lines up with continuous batching + prefix cache attempts where the runtime blocks on write for a few cycles then aborts to preserve worker health. We currently abort after ~3 blocked write iterations to avoid thread starvation.

Lin: Related note — the customer saw a 401 on reconnects. That's probably their short-lived token expired between the disconnect and their reconnect attempt. Might be a client-side re-auth race.

Arjun: Two parts here: 1) server aborts to protect the worker (we throttle on backpressure), 2) client reconnect flow + auth token expiry causing failed reconnections and duplicate sessions -> billing. Need repro steps.

Maya: Customer provided a minimal repro using node + express with a delayed consumer. Repro gist:
```
// client.js
const es = new EventSource('/stream');
es.onmessage = (e) => { console.log('chunk', e.data); setTimeout(()=>{/* slow processing */}, 2500); }
```
and server produces a chunk every 200ms. After ~4-6 chunks we hit runtime abort.
```
// curl repro
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream?model=x
```

Tomas: Can reproduce locally with the same timing. On my laptop I see write stalls and then the worker logs the same abort message. Adding TCP_NODELAY helps slightly but the fundamental problem is the runtime's write buffer fill + our conservative abort threshold.

Arjun: What about the edge/proxy? Are we doing any buffering at the edge that could amplify this?

deploy-bot: Edge config: envoy buffer_size=8k per-stream; proxy idle timeouts: 15s; streaming passthrough enabled.

Lin: If the proxy buffers, the runtime may think client accepted bytes while the client hasn't processed them yet (because proxy acked), making our backpressure signals tricky. But logs show EAGAIN on write — that's the kernel telling us the socket buffer is full, so the client or proxy isn't draining.

Maya: Customer also noted a billing spike: because their client retries immediately on any close, and the reconnect sometimes succeeds with a new token, they get charged for multiple partial sessions. They want guidance to avoid wasted tokens/requests.

Tomas: Short-term mitigations:
- increase write retry window to 6 iterations (was 3)
- add explicit SSE keepalive small chunk every 1s to keep some flow moving
- surface a header X-Stream-Backpressure to clients so they can detect slow-consumer and pause

Arjun: Longer-term: implement graceful slow-consumer throttling rather than abort: slow down chunk rate per-connection, fall back to polling or smaller chunk sizes, and add a client-side backoff header we can inspect.

Lin: For the auth-related reconnects: advise customers to use refresh tokens with background refresh, or extend session validity for streaming flows. Also update our docs with a recommended reconnect strategy: exponential backoff + check 401 -> refresh token before immediate reconnect.

Maya: I drafted an initial customer response. Please review before I send.

Maya (draft reply): Hi — thanks for the report. We reproduced this locally. Short version: when a client is very slow to read SSE chunks, the server-side socket buffer fills and our runtime currently aborts the stream to protect the worker. This can cause the client to reconnect quickly and, if the token expires during the reconnect window, fail with 401 and then retry again, creating duplicate charges.

Action items we propose:
1) Immediate: Tell client to implement exponential backoff on reconnects and refresh tokens in the background (doc link).
2) Near-term (config change): We'll raise the write-abort threshold for your tenant and enable a keepalive chunk to reduce aborts while you evaluate. (no downtime)
3) Mid-term: We're tracking runtime improvements to do per-connection pacing to avoid hard aborts.

Would you like us to push the tenant config change now?

Arjun: +1, push config change for this tenant, set abort_threshold=6 and enable keepalive=1s. I'll monitor worker CPU and queued writes.

Tomas: I'll open a runtime PR to change the default to be more tolerant and add metrics: backpressure_block_count and aborted_for_backpressure. Also will add a small note in the streaming docs for recommended client-side patterns.

Lin: I'll update the support KB with an SSE troubleshooting checklist: curl repro, set TCP_NODELAY, token refresh guidance, and recommended client reconnect backoff snippet.

Maya: Sending the customer the draft now and scheduling a quick runbook review with Arjun and Tomas. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Arjun: Follow-up: I found a small log line we can add to make triage faster: log connection drain percentage and last_write_error when we call abort. Will add to PR.

Tomas: FYI repro command I used:
```
node repro/slow_consumer.js --rate 200 --process-delay 2500
# shows the EAGAIN/EPIPE sequence reliably in ~5s
```

Maya: Closing loop here. I will post the customer's acceptance after config change and attach the updated KB link.
